# Staying Up-to-Date: The Live Intelligence Layer

## Problem
Test formats, interfaces, and item types change frequently without notice (especially corporate psychometric and IT cert exams). Static question banks become obsolete quickly.

## Solution: A Living Product Model
Capture → Analyze → Re-template → Re-simulate → Release update  
(Community/extension/scanning) → (AI flags novelty) → (Designer adjusts templates) → (Engine regenerates questions + updates UI skins) → (Pushed to users within days)

## Components of the Live Intelligence Layer

### 1. Community-Powered Intelligence Flywheel
Users are the best sensors. After taking a real test, they provide structured feedback via in-app "Post-Test Debrief Form."
- Fields: Test provider, role, interface look-and-feel (dropdowns), new question types observed, time pressure, number of questions, difficulty, optional screenshots.
- Incentives: Free premium days, badges, micro-rewards for verified useful intel.
- Community channels: Discord/Reddit "Intel" groups where test-takers share observations. Research team mines daily.

### 2. EyeWitness Browser Extension (Passive, Opt-In)
For online-proctored tests, with user consent, a lightweight extension captures:
- Visual fingerprint: UI structure, button placements, color schemes, navigation flow, timer behavior (not question content).
- Detection of new interaction widgets (drag-and-drop graphs, 3D rotation).
- Timing cadence (section durations, transitions).
Data is anonymized, stripped of personal info, aggregated. Legal if no content stored. Enables rapid UI replication.

### 3. Continuous External Signal Mining
Automated scanning of public signals:
- Job description changes (announcing new assessment partners).
- Glassdoor & Reddit reviews (sentiment/keyword extraction for changes).
- Test publisher press releases & patent filings (early warning of new formats).

### 4. Rapid-Response Content Pipeline (Why Templates Win)
AI question engine uses generative rule sets. When intel arrives:
- Add/adjust template rules (e.g., new chart type for numerical tests).
- Engine produces 500 fresh versions immediately.
No manual writing needed.

### 5. Adaptive Simulator – Not Just Static Mock
Configurable simulation engine that morphs interface on the fly.
- "Explorer Mode" updates UI weekly based on community intel, with note: "Our latest intelligence suggests the real test now uses a 4-panel split screen."
- Users provide immediate feedback: "Yes, that's exactly what I saw!" → lock as default.

### 6. Formal Partnerships (Long Game)
Partner with test publishers or large corporate recruiters to become an authorized preparation platform.
- Offer: "We'll create a white-labeled practice environment matching your test's look and feel, using AI-generated non-live content."
- Gives official UI specs and change logs – ultimate defense against fluidity.

### 7. Resilience Through Aggregation
Even if temporarily behind a new interface, your tool trains the underlying cognitive skills. Users are still better prepared than those who only memorized old banks. Builds trust that your tool improves scores, not just familiarity.

## Operational Model Summary
The platform becomes a **living product**, not static. This is the opposite of JobTestPrep/AssessmentDay which push annual updates. Your brand becomes known as *the* tool always in sync with the real test – a defensible premium position.
